competitive_landscape: Run by the Steamship Authority (the lifeline operator) plus Hy-Line Cruises and seasonal fast ferries — all diesel, with severe summer peak-demand congestion and well-publicised reliability strain. No premium all-electric tier exists.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Almost the entire network — Woods Hole/Falmouth ↔ the Vineyard (~3–7nm) and Hyannis ↔ Nantucket (~23nm) — sits inside Pioneer II range, an ideal all-electric premium layer over a congested diesel ferry system.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Not required; the Sound crossings are well within Pioneer II range.

precedents.why_it_matters: A US commercial reference for the N30 — directly relevant to a high-volume US ferry corridor.

regulatory_note: US-flagged passenger operations fall under USCG inspection (Subchapter T) and the Jones Act for domestic carriage; coordination with the Steamship Authority and Massachusetts DOT. Nantucket/Vineyard Sound has eelgrass and protected-species considerations that favour zero-wake operation.
seasonality: Intense Jun–Sep peak with sold-out reservations; quieter shoulder/winter lifeline service. Nantucket Sound is exposed and fog-prone — foiling adds stability and schedule resilience.
summary: The Cape Cod & Islands network links Woods Hole, Hyannis and Falmouth on the mainland to Martha's Vineyard (Vineyard Haven, Oak Bluffs) and Nantucket. In summer it is one of the busiest passenger-ferry systems in the United States, with heavy peak-day congestion and a strong decarbonisation push.
tagline: Martha's Vineyard, Nantucket and the Cape — one of America's densest seasonal ferry networks.
